Rank order is EVIDENCE-LED: the lymphoedema edge is ranked first because its primary anchor names the complication in its own background and supplies paired response magnitudes, the thromboembolism edge is second because it is the only one with a pooled soft-tissue-specific proportion, and the anaemia edge is third because its quantitative anchor is a single-centre retroperitoneal subset and its second anchor is expert consensus resting on indirect evidence.

UMDRELLA GUARD, APPLIED ACROSS ALL THREE EDGES: this identity is a family concept and the catalog holds at least three narrower members of it as separate identities, dermatofibrosarcoma-protuberans, gastrointestinal-stromal-tumors and kaposi-s-sarcoma. All three batch-86 targets are therefore deliberately chosen to lie OUTSIDE that family so that no edge is registered between an identity and its own sub-identities, and any individual claim MUST document the exact sarcoma subtype and site rather than citing this identity generically.

No magnitude is stated for the lymphoedema edge, because both of its anchors are treatment series selected for patients who already have the complication. The thromboembolism edge carries magnitudes that are PROPORTIONS AMONG SURGICALLY TREATED PATIENTS, not population incidence, its bone-versus-soft-tissue difference is not statistically significant, and its network meta-analysis found no prophylaxis strategy with a significant effect. The anaemia edge carries an up-to-40-percent preoperative prevalence from one institution's retroperitoneal subset only, alongside a recorded null on malnutrition in the same cohort.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Extensive resection of a soft tissue sarcoma, particularly in a lymphatic high-risk region such as the medial thigh or the groin, removes or disrupts a large volume of lymphatic drainage territory, and postoperative lymphorrhea and secondary lymphedema are the recognised consequences. A retrospective series of 24 patients who underwent secondary lymphaticovenular anastomosis after lower-extremity soft tissue sarcoma resection between 2019 and 2024 states in its own background that extensive resection of lower-extremity soft tissue sarcoma, particularly in the medial thigh and groin, is FREQUENTLY ASSOCIATED with postoperative lymphorrhea and secondary lymphedema; lymphaticovenular anastomosis was performed for lymphorrhea in 16 patients and for lymphedema in 8, median per-patient five-day mean daily drainage volume fell from 250.0 mL/day before anastomosis to 82.0 mL/day after it (p LESS THAN 0.01), and in the six lymphedema patients with complete paired data the lower-extremity lymphedema Index fell from a median of 258.0 to 241.1 mL/day (exact two-sided p EQUALS 0.031) (PMID 42561503). A case report of a 53-year-old man who underwent wide resection of a left medial-thigh myxoid liposarcoma with femoral artery and vein resection, contralateral small saphenous vein graft and a pedicled rectus abdominis musculocutaneous flap, developed profuse refractory lymphorrhea and lower-extremity oedema; after two-compartment lymphoscintigraphy localised deep-system leakage near the femoral canal resection margin, further anastomoses reduced drain output from approximately 200 to 19 mL/day within seven days with complete resolution of leakage on repeat lymphoscintigraphy and no recurrence within 94 days (PMID 42656561). Recorded as documented association only, with the fact that both anchors are TREATMENT series for a post-resection lymphatic complication and neither reports an incidence, carried openly.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established for any individual, and NEITHER ANCHOR REPORTS AN INCIDENCE OR A RISK for lymphedema after soft tissue sarcoma resection, because both are therapeutic series selected for patients who already had the complication. The primary anchor's lymphedema arm contains only six patients with complete paired data out of a total of 24, and the authors themselves direct that the clinical outcome findings be interpreted in light of the retrospective design and the small subgroup sizes; its reduction in the lower-extremity lymphedema Index is therefore a treatment response in already-affected patients, not an effect of the sarcoma. The second anchor is a SINGLE CASE with a 94-day follow-up, which cannot support any frequency statement, and its deep anastomosis technique is a management report rather than an aetiological observation. The relation is registered as a POST-SURGICAL_OR_TREATMENT vector: surgical lymphatic disruption is the hypothesised route, and it is labelled hypothesizedOnly because the located evidence establishes the association only inside patients who were referred for lymphatic surgery, which is a selected population. Individual claims require a dated sarcoma resection with the resection site and lymphatic risk region documented, postoperative drain output and limb circumference measured serially rather than inferred, lymphoscintigraphy or other confirmatory lymphatic imaging, and a clinical determination separating resection-related lymphatic disruption from tumour infiltration, prior surgery, radiation, infection and obesity, each of which applies in this population at substantial rates.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: The hypothesised vector is surgical disruption of a contiguous lymphatic network: wide oncological resection of a soft tissue sarcoma removes subcutaneous lymphatics, nodes and channels in an en bloc specimen, and the divided lymphatic outflow from the resected skin and subcutaneous territory then has to drain across the new surgical margin, so drainage volume rises and limb volume rises with it; the vector is named as the resection and its lymphatic disruption rather than as the tumour's own biology, because the located anchors are all treatment reports for a post-resection complication and none separates the resection's contribution from the disease's.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at retrospective-treatment-series and single-case-report class, following the file's existing oncologic and treatment-related (iatrogenic) pathway scope. The series is the anchor that supplies the mechanism and the response magnitudes, 24 patients, 16 treated for lymphorrhea and 8 for lymphedema, drainage 250.0 to 82.0 mL/day and a lower-extremity lymphedema Index median of 258.0 to 241.1, and its six-patient lymphedema subgroup is disclosed on the face of the edge (PMID 42561503). The case report is registered because it is the located source that shows the complication persisting after an initial superficial-system lymphatic intervention and resolving after deep-system intervention, which is the specific finding that makes the deep-versus-superficial distinction in the mechanism claim necessary (PMID 42656561). Because both anchors are selected on the presence of the complication and neither supplies a denominator for all resected patients, the conservative standard holds the edge at association only and states no magnitude for the population.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Malignancy and major oncological surgery are both recognised drivers of venous thromboembolism, and the located orthopaedic-oncology literature supplies pooled, site-stratified estimates for surgically treated sarcoma. A PRISMA systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis of 34 studies comprising 85,425 patients and 2,283 venous thromboembolism events estimated a POOLED VENOUS THROMBOEMBOLISM PROPORTION OF 4.5 PERCENT (95% CI 3.2 to 6.3) among surgically treated sarcoma patients, with a soft tissue sarcoma subgroup of 3.4 percent (95% CI 1.5 to 7.9) against 4.3 percent (95% CI 2.9 to 6.4) for bone sarcoma and no statistically significant difference between them (p EQUALS 0.57); substantial heterogeneity was present (tau-squared 1.24; I-squared 94.5 percent), and a network meta-analysis of 2,556 observations across eight prophylaxis strategies found NO strategy with a statistically significant VTE reduction relative to no prophylaxis (PMID 42471349). A propensity-matched retrospective cohort of 1,223 patients undergoing retroperitoneal tumour surgery found venous thromboembolism in 2.1 percent, with age (odds ratio 1.140, 95% CI 1.053 to 1.239, p EQUALS 0.004), recurrence (odds ratio 1.851, 95% CI 1.241 to 2.761, p EQUALS 0.003) and vascular resection (odds ratio 2.036, 95% CI 1.054 to 3.934, p EQUALS 0.034) as independent risk factors, and inferior overall survival in the thromboembolism group (hazard ratio 2.090, 95% CI 1.014 to 4.308, p EQUALS 0.046) (PMID 37578462). A Pediatric Health Information System analysis of 2,400 patients aged 18 and under discharged 2004 to 2015 after lower-extremity sarcoma resection found 19 venous thromboembolism events, 0.79 percent, with 1.4 percent (95% CI 0.5 to 3.2) for pelvic tumours and 0.6 percent (95% CI 0.3 to 1.0) for lower-limb tumours, an event count the authors state was too rare to permit risk-factor analysis (PMID 36693390). Recorded as documented association only, with the fact that the surgical literature reports PROPORTIONS IN SELECTED SURGICAL COHORTS rather than population incidence, carried openly.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established for any individual, and the located estimates are PROPORTIONS AMONG SURGICALLY TREATED PATIENTS rather than population incidence, so a claim cannot present 3.4 percent or 4.5 percent as this identity's risk in an unselected population. The primary anchor's heterogeneity is very high (I-squared 94.5 percent), its own authors note that the pooled 4.5 percent is LOWER than some previously cited estimates and should be read in light of heterogeneity and variable study quality, and its network meta-analysis found NO prophylaxis strategy with a significant reduction, so the edge cannot be used to imply that a recognised prophylaxis prevents the events. The second anchor is a retroperitoneal-TUMOUR cohort in which sarcoma appears only as a between-group characteristic and is not separately analysed, so its 2.1 percent is a retroperitoneal-tumour figure and not a soft tissue sarcoma figure; its hazard ratio for overall survival is an association with death in patients who already had an event and is not a causal effect of the thrombosis. The third anchor is a PEDIATRIC database study of a lower-extremity malignant neoplasm category combining bone and soft tissue, so it neither describes an adult soft tissue sarcoma population nor separates the two histologies, and its authors state the event count precluded formal analysis. Individual claims require a dated sarcoma diagnosis with histology and site documented, a dated thromboembolic event confirmed on imaging, a documented surgical and immobilisation history, and a clinical determination separating the tumour's contribution from that of surgery, venous injury, central venous access, immobility and inherited thrombophilia, all of which the located anchors do not partition.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: The hypothesised vector is a combined cancer-associated prothrombotic state with perioperative venous stasis: the tumour and its treatments raise inflammatory mediators and activate coagulation and endothelium, while major pelvic, retroperitoneal and lower-limb resection produces venous injury, reduced calf-muscle pump activity and prolonged immobilisation, and those two drivers compound rather than substitute for one another; the vector is named as the tumour-and-surgery combination rather than as either alone because no located anchor partitions the two contributions, and because the pooled analysis found no prophylaxis strategy with a significant effect, which is itself consistent with a multifactorial rather than a single-modifiable-driver model.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at systematic-review-and-meta-analysis, propensity-matched-retrospective-cohort and national-administrative-database class, following the file's existing vascular and oncological pathway scope. The meta-analysis is the anchor that supplies the soft-tissue-specific magnitude and the direct bone-versus-soft-tissue comparison, 3.4 percent against 4.3 percent with p EQUALS 0.57 across 85,425 patients and 2,283 events, and both its very high heterogeneity and its null prophylaxis result are stated on the face of the edge rather than omitted (PMID 42471349). The propensity-matched cohort is registered because it is the located source that identifies age, recurrence and VASCULAR RESECTION as independent predictors and reports inferior overall survival in the thromboembolism group, which is the finding that makes the surgical component of the mechanism claim concrete, and its population is a retroperitoneal-tumour cohort in which sarcoma is a between-group characteristic rather than an analysed stratum, which is disclosed (PMID 37578462). The paediatric database analysis is registered for its contrasting null, 0.79 percent overall, which bounds the edge and shows the pooled surgical estimate is not universal across populations (PMID 36693390). Because all three are selected surgical or administrative cohorts and none partitions tumour from surgery, the conservative standard holds the edge at association only.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: ALL THREE ANCHORS ARE SELECTED SURGICAL OR ADMINISTRATIVE COHORTS, so every figure is a PROPORTION AMONG TREATED PATIENTS and not population incidence, and no located anchor reports an unselected soft tissue sarcoma venous thromboembolism rate (PMID 42471349, PMID 37578462, PMID 36693390). THE PRIMARY ANCHOR'S HETEROGENEITY IS VERY HIGH (tau-squared 1.24, I-squared 94.5 PERCENT), its authors state that the pooled 4.5 percent is lower than some previously cited estimates and should be interpreted in light of heterogeneity and variable study quality, and the bone-versus-soft-tissue difference of 4.3 against 3.4 percent is NOT statistically significant (p EQUALS 0.57) (PMID 42471349). THE PRIMARY ANCHOR'S NETWORK META-ANALYSIS FOUND NO PROPHYLAXIS STRATEGY with a statistically significant reduction in venous thromboembolism relative to no prophylaxis, so the edge cannot be used to imply that an established intervention prevents the events (PMID 42471349). NO located anchor partitions the tumour's contribution from that of surgery, venous injury, immobilisation, central venous access or inherited thrombophilia, and no located anchor reports an event rate in patients treated non-surgically.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Anaemia is a common and prognostically loaded finding in the sarcoma surgical population, and the located evidence reports both its frequency and its trajectory. A retrospective longitudinal cohort of 370 patients undergoing resection of primary or recurrent retroperitoneal soft tissue sarcoma at a single university hospital found that PREOPERATIVE ANAEMIA AFFECTED UP TO 40 PERCENT of patients, that haemoglobin levels SIGNIFICANTLY DECREASED OVER THE COURSE OF THE DISEASE (p EQUALS 0.022) and that the decrease correlated significantly with the NUMBER OF TUMOUR RESECTIONS PERFORMED (p EQUALS 0.010); low preoperative haemoglobin was associated with increased 30-day mortality and was identified as an INDEPENDENT PROGNOSTIC FACTOR for shorter overall survival in primary retroperitoneal sarcoma as well as in second and third recurrences, leading the authors to recommend preoperative anaemia screening and screening at regular follow-up (PMID 39841283). A modified-Delphi consensus guideline for perioperative care in primary retroperitoneal sarcoma surgery, developed under the Spanish Society of Surgeons and the Portuguese Sarcoma Group with systematic literature review and four structured voting rounds, proposed 42 recommendations of which 33 reached consensus, 17 with weak consensus and 16 with strong, and in which PREOPERATIVE ANAEMIA CORRECTION appears alongside smoking cessation and nutritional optimisation as an explicit preoperative recommendation (PMID 41973294). The same cohort reports the contrasting null that it observed NEITHER A SIGNIFICANT PREVALENCE OF PREOPERATIVE MALNUTRITION NOR NOTABLE CHANGES in body mass index or serum albumin across the disease course (PMID 39841283). Recorded as documented association only, with the fact that the strongest anchor is a single-centre retrospective cohort restricted to a retroperitoneal subset, carried openly.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established for any individual, and the 40 percent figure is a PREOPERATIVE PREVALENCE IN A RETROPERITONEAL SOFT TISSUE SARCOMA COHORT at one institution, so it cannot be transferred to soft tissue sarcomas at other sites, to other histologies, or to an unselected population. The primary anchor is retrospective and single-centre, and its independent-prognosis finding is an adjusted ASSOCIATION with mortality rather than evidence that correcting anaemia improves any outcome; its own recommendation to screen and treat early is framed as a potential strategy, not a demonstrated intervention effect. The second anchor is a consensus guideline rather than a primary study, and its recommendations are explicitly noted by its authors to be supported largely by INDIRECT evidence from major abdominal surgery, with 9 of 42 proposals failing to reach the predefined consensus threshold, so it establishes that preoperative anaemia correction is considered appropriate practice rather than that anaemia causes any specific outcome in this identity. The contrasting null on malnutrition is recorded because it prevents the anaemia finding from being read as a marker of general nutritional depletion in this cohort. Individual claims require a dated sarcoma diagnosis with site and histology documented, serial haemoglobin measurements with the transfusion history and the resection count recorded alongside them, an assessment of the specific cause of any anaemia, and a clinical determination separating tumour-associated and treatment-associated anaemia from occult blood loss, chronic inflammation of another origin, renal impairment, iron or vitamin deficiency and bone marrow involvement.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: The hypothesised vector is cumulative physiological and operative burden rather than a single lesion: repeated wide resections of a sarcoma produce serial blood loss, repeated periods of fasting and catabolic stress and repeated exposure to anaemia-generating therapy, so red-cell mass is consumed faster than it is replaced, and each further resection is reported to correlate with a further fall in haemoglobin; the vector is named as the cumulative resection and treatment burden rather than as the tumour's direct suppression of erythropoiesis because the located anchors are clinical cohorts that do not separate those contributions, and the recorded null on albumin and body mass index argues against reading the anaemia as a marker of generalised malnutrition.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at single-centre-retrospective-longitudinal-cohort and modified-Delphi-consensus-guideline class, following the file's existing oncologic, haematological and treatment-related (iatrogenic) pathway scope. The cohort is the anchor that supplies the frequency, the trajectory and the adjusted prognostic signal, 370 patients, preoperative anaemia in up to 40 percent, haemoglobin falling across the disease course with p EQUALS 0.022 and correlating with resection count at p EQUALS 0.010, and it is also the anchor for the malnutrition null, which is carried onto the face of the edge so that the anaemia finding is not over-read (PMID 39841283). The consensus guideline is registered because it is the located source that places preoperative anaemia correction within an expert consensus perioperative pathway for this specific surgery, and its indirect-evidence basis and its 9 non-consensus proposals are disclosed rather than presented as trial evidence (PMID 41973294). Because the only quantitative anchor is a single-centre retrospective cohort in one anatomical subset and the second anchor is expert opinion, the conservative standard holds the edge at association only and refuses to state a magnitude for soft tissue sarcoma outside that subset.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: THE ONLY QUANTITATIVE ANCHOR IS A SINGLE-CENTRE RETROPERPERITONEAL COHORT, so the up-to-40-percent preoperative prevalence describes one institution's retroperitoneal subset and cannot be transferred to other sarcoma sites, other histologies or an unselected population (PMID 39841283). THE PRIMARY ANCHOR IS RETROSPECTIVE and its finding that low preoperative haemoglobin is an independent prognostic factor is an ADJUSTED ASSOCIATION WITH MORTALITY, not evidence that correcting anaemia changes any outcome; the authors frame early screening and treatment as a potential strategy rather than a demonstrated intervention (PMID 39841283). THE SECOND ANCHOR IS AN EXPERT CONSENSUS GUIDELINE, NOT A PRIMARY STUDY: 33 of 42 recommendations reached consensus, 17 of them only weakly, 9 did not reach the predefined threshold, and the authors state that most recommendations are supported by INDIRECT evidence from major abdominal surgery (PMID 41973294). THE PRIMARY ANCHOR REPORTS A CONTRADICTORY NULL on nutrition: NEITHER A SIGNIFICANT PREVALENCE OF PREOPERATIVE MALNUTRITION NOR NOTABLE CHANGES in body mass index or serum albumin across the disease course, which is recorded here so that this anaemia edge is not read as evidence of generalised nutritional depletion in the same cohort (PMID 39841283). NO located anchor separates the tumour's contribution from that of serial resection, blood loss, anaemia-generating therapy, occult gastrointestinal bleeding, chronic inflammation of another origin, renal impairment, iron or vitamin deficiency, or bone marrow involvement, and no located anchor reports the anaemia rate for non-retroperitoneal soft tissue sarcoma sites.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Occult or overt blood loss from the tumour or from the operative field, which in a sarcoma resection is substantial and which the located cohort does not separate from the other drivers
Anaemia-generating oncological therapy, including cytotoxic regimens and radiotherapy, whose contribution is not partitioned in any located anchor
Chronic inflammation of a non-tumour origin and renal impairment, both of which produce anaemia independently and both of which are common in this population
Iron, vitamin B12 or folate deficiency from reduced intake, which the located cohort's null on albumin and body mass index neither supports nor excludes
Bone marrow involvement or infiltration, which would give the anaemia a wholly different mechanism and which must be excluded before the edge is applied to an individual

suggestions.rationale: Authoring registers this edge because preoperative anaemia is the one haematological finding the located sarcoma cohorts both quantify and connect to outcome, and because the target identity, anemia, is the most heavily targeted identity in the registry at 28 incoming edges while this catalog identity had ZERO. The conservative framing is explicit that the quantitative anchor is a single-centre retroperitoneal subset, that the second anchor is expert consensus resting on indirect evidence, and that the same cohort reports a null on malnutrition which is carried on the edge.

sourceReferences.citation: Willis F, Trunk AM, Musa J, et al. Temporal variation in nutritional status and preoperative anemia among patients with retroperitoneal soft tissue sarcoma: a retrospective longitudinal cohort study. Langenbecks Arch Surg. 2025 Jan 22;410(1):48. doi: 10.1007/s00423-024-03585-5. PMID 39841283.
sourceReferences.note: Retrospective longitudinal cohort of 370 patients undergoing resection of primary or recurrent retroperitoneal SOFT TISSUE SARCOMA at a single university hospital, analysed with hierarchical linear regression for haemoglobin and nutritional trajectories and multivariable Cox regression for survival. PREOPERATIVE ANAEMIA AFFECTED UP TO 40 PERCENT of patients; haemoglobin DECREASED SIGNIFICANTLY ACROSS THE DISEASE COURSE (p EQUALS 0.022) and the decrease correlated with the NUMBER OF TUMOUR RESECTIONS (p EQUALS 0.010); low preoperative haemoglobin was associated with increased 30-day mortality and was an INDEPENDENT PROGNOSTIC FACTOR for shorter overall survival in primary disease and in second and third recurrences. CONTRADICTORY NULL RECORDED ON THE EDGE: the authors observed NEITHER A SIGNIFICANT PREVALENCE OF PREOPERATIVE MALNUTRITION NOR NOTABLE CHANGES in body mass index or serum albumin across the disease course, and recommend preoperative and follow-up anaemia screening. Registered as the sole quantitative anchor for this edge; its single-centre retroperitoneal scope and its retrospective design are disclosed on the face of the edge.
sourceReferences.sourceLocator: Langenbecks Arch Surg. 2025;410(1):48. Retrospective longitudinal cohort of 370 resected retroperitoneal soft tissue sarcoma patients: preoperative anaemia in up to 40 percent, haemoglobin declining across the disease course and with resection count, and low preoperative haemoglobin an independent prognostic factor for overall survival.

sourceReferences.citation: Lominchar PL, Díaz-Cambronero Ó, Muñoz-Muñoz P, et al. Consensus Guidelines on Perioperative Care in Primary Retroperitoneal Sarcoma Surgery. Ann Surg Oncol. 2026 Jul;33(7):6881-6909. doi: 10.1245/s10434-026-19520-5. PMID 41973294.
sourceReferences.note: Modified-Delphi consensus guideline on perioperative care in primary retroperitoneal sarcoma surgery, developed under the Spanish Society of Surgeons and the Portuguese Sarcoma Group with a systematic literature review, subgroup synthesis and four structured voting rounds; consensus was defined as 80 percent or greater agreement and strength was graded with GRADE. 42 recommendations were proposed across preoperative care, including PREOPERATIVE ANAEMIA CORRECTION, smoking cessation and nutritional optimisation; 33 reached consensus, 17 of them with weak consensus and 16 with strong, while 9 did not meet the predefined threshold. The authors state that most recommendations are supported by INDIRECT evidence from major abdominal surgery. Registered as the located source that places preoperative anaemia correction within an expert consensus perioperative pathway for this specific operation. DISCLOSED: this is EXPERT CONSENSUM RATHER THAN PRIMARY EVIDENCE, its recommendations rest on indirect evidence, and it cannot establish that anaemia causes any specific outcome in this identity or that correcting it changes one.

governanceNotes: IDENTITY SCREEN, batch 86: no alias duplication found. Catalog siblings dermatofibrosarcoma-protuberans, gastrointestinal-stromal-tumors and kaposi-s-sarcoma share the soft-tissue sarcoma family in several classification schemes but carry no alias overlap with this identity, and no edge has been registered between this identity and any of them, because such an edge would be a taxonomic containment rather than a secondary condition.

INCOMING-EDGE MAP, batch 86: this identity had ZERO registered incoming edges and ZERO registered outgoing edges before this batch, so all three edges are new and none duplicates an existing relationship. Target identities with thin prior coverage were preferred, including lymphedema at 4 incoming edges and deep-vein-thrombosis at 7, while anemia at 28 was selected only because the located evidence for it is the strongest of the haematological candidates.

ERRATUM DISCLOSURE: the primary lymphoedema anchor (PMID 42561503) is flagged by the source-status preflight as an erratum-linked record, with a notice in J Plast Reconstr Aesthet Surg. 2026 Oct;121:152, doi 10.1016/j.bjps.2026.08.011. The notice is NOT a retraction, expression of concern or withdrawal, and its content was NOT checked in this authoring pass. A qualified-human verifier must read the erratum before this reference is relied on for anything beyond the direction of the association.

TWO EDGES REST ON ANCHORS THAT DO NOT STUDY THEIR OWN TARGET CATEGORY DIRECTLY and both are disclosed on the face of the edge: the thromboembolism second anchor is a retroperitoneal-tumour cohort in which sarcoma is a between-group characteristic only, and the lymphoedema second anchor is a single case with 94 days of follow-up that supports a mechanism observation and no frequency statement.
